transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Sam P (Redwood AE), Priya R (Redwood SE), Alex M (Redwood SE), Marcus L (Atlas Head of ML), Sara G (Platform Eng), Priya A (CTO)

00:00 Sam Patel: all right, hey everyone thanks for joining, should we do a quick round-robin intro?
00:08 Marcus Lee: yep Marcus here, head of ML at Atlas, we own the inference stack and run a mix of hosted APIs and some self-hosted endpoints, curious about the Optimize piece.
00:15 Sara Gomez: Sara, platform eng, I'll be looking at the ops side and cost impact.
00:21 Priya Anand: Priya, CTO, interested in security and the SLA implications.
00:26 Priya Rao: thanks, quick agenda: we'll walk through batching basics, prefix and KV cache patterns, show the cost model and some heuristics for batch sizes, then wrap with pilot next steps.
00:38 Alex Moretti: quick note, today's demo will use a synthetic traffic profile similar to what Marcus shared previously, but if you send logs we'll run a dedicated run later.
00:47 Sam Patel: right, ok jumping into batching, basic idea is grouping concurrent requests to amortize per-step kernel overhead, best for smaller inputs or high qps. tradeoff is added queuing latency.
01:05 Marcus Lee: can you quantify that? our p99 SLA is tight, under 200ms for small requests, so queuing sounds risky.
01:13 Priya Rao: yup, good question. for p50-focused workloads you can get 2-3x token throughput with batching of 8-16, but p99 latency degrades if you let latencies accumulate. Redwood Optimize suggests dynamic batch windows: small immediate flush for >p95, and opportunistic batching for p50/p90. we showed the chart - at batch size 8 median cost per token drops ~40% but p99 increases ~60ms in our sim.
01:45 Sara Gomez: ok that's helpful. how does KV cache interact with batching?
01:52 Alex Moretti: KV/prefix cache reduces computation by reusing cached KV states for repeated prefixes - especially in chat or instruction-heavy workloads. if you have high prefix reuse, effective tokens/second goes way up and batching becomes even cheaper because fewer compute steps needed.
02:10 Marcus Lee: our docs app has a lot of repeated prompts and a few hundred top templates, so prefix reuse is high. what hit rates should we expect?
02:18 Priya Rao: depends on cardinality and TTL. with a 72-hour window and our LRU profile we often see 60-80% hit on template-driven workloads. for your workload we'd expect 50-70% initially, improving as cache warms.
02:33 Marcus Lee: and cost model? can you show numbers?
02:36 Sam Patel: yes we walked through the cost model: baseline hosted cost X per 1M tokens, with batching and KV cache you can reduce effective cost per token by 30-60% depending on hit rate and batch size. we shared a spreadsheet (link in chat) - example: at batch=8 and cache hit 60% cost drops ~45% vs no-optimizations.
03:02 Sara Gomez: there's always the question of dedicated vs hosted - how much of this relies on dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput?
03:09 Priya Rao: you can get benefits on hosted as well; the main difference is SLO predictability. Dedicated pools give you fixed throughput and tighter p99 control with fixed queueing knobs. hosted uses smart routing and burst capacity but might have more variable tail latencies under contention.
03:28 Priya Anand: security - are keys and cache stored in our VPC for private deployment? audit logs?
03:35 Alex Moretti: yes for Redwood Private we offer customer-managed networking and options to store KVs and checkpoints in your KMS-controlled storage. audit logs are available and we integrate with KMS/HSM for key control. SOC 2 and ISO docs we can share.
03:50 Marcus Lee: one concern - mis-specified caching could leak PII across tenants. how do you prevent that?
03:58 Priya Rao: great catch. caches are tenant-scoped by default; we never share KV across tenants. for sensitive data we recommend cache disable for sensitive endpoints or encrypt at rest plus strict TTLs. we also support tokenization and PII detection hooks pre-cache.
04:20 Sam Patel: returning to cost, another lever is quantization and reduced-precision execution; that stacks with batching and cache. Atlas, do you run INT8 weights today?
04:30 Marcus Lee: we experimented but didn't push to prod.
04:33 Priya Rao: our recommendations: start with 16-bit, enable KV cache and conservative batching (batch 4) for canary, measure p99 and user-facing latency, then increase batch size if p99 acceptable and cache hit rate stable.
04:50 Sara Gomez: what about burst traffic? during peak end of month we get spikes 3-4x baseline.
04:56 Alex Moretti: we advise a mixed policy: reserve capacity for baseline (dedicated or reserved hosted) and allow autoscaling/burst for peaks. Optimize will suggest split routing by policy and fallback to smaller model variant if capacity constrained.
05:15 Marcus Lee: demos look promising. any concrete pilot suggestion?
05:19 Sam Patel: pilot: 2-week run using a reserved pool + hosted fallback, Redwood to run simulation on your request logs, measure cost-per-100k tokens and p95/p99; we provide config: batch window, max batch size, cache TTL recommendations.
05:33 Priya Anand: ok that sounds reasonable. timeline?
05:36 Sam Patel: we'll send the costing spreadsheet and sample configs by Friday, schedule the benchmark next week, and aim to have pilot data in two weeks.
05:46 Sara Gomez: please include the exact API route configs and SDK examples for Node/Python.
05:51 Priya Rao: will do - also include a small script to replay traffic into a dedicated pool.
05:58 Marcus Lee: a few small clarifications in the transcript - you said 60-80% hit earlier, can you show the math?
06:03 Alex Moretti: yes in the spreadsheet there's a breakdown: effective token compute = tokens * (1 - hit_rate) + metadata overhead; we included amortized batch savings and KV deserialization costs. but simple rule: each 10% increase in hit-rate yields ~8-12% effective cost reduction depending on model size.
06:24 Sam Patel: recap of action items and owners, and we'll share SOC2 and KMS integration docs. any other blockers?
06:32 Priya Anand: just need legal review on storage of embeddings and cache eviction policy, but initial ask looks fine.
06:38 Marcus Lee: ok thanks everyone, looking forward to the spreadsheet and benchmark.
06:42 Sam Patel: thanks all, end of call.
